How brokers can support new agents without overspending

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (865 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housingwire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, I believe a lot of brokers really miss the mark when it comes to supporting their agents, and in the long run, that hurts them just as much as it hurts agents.
  • It has been revealed that think about it like this — you meet an agent who has the right mindset, but they don’t yet have the experience or confidence to come out of the gates running.
  • It has been revealed that broker A adopts a sink or swim approach, forcing them to learn the job on the fly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, I believe a lot of brokers really miss the mark when it comes to supporting their agents, and in the long run, that hurts them just as much as it hurts agents. They treat things like education and mentorship like a cost, rather than an investment, so they miss out on a lot of agents who had the potential to become top producers.

It has been revealed that think about it like this — you meet an agent who has the right mindset, but they don’t yet have the experience or confidence to come out of the gates running. You hire them anyway.

It has been revealed that broker A adopts a sink or swim approach, forcing them to learn the job on the fly. After all, they’ve already learned the technical side in their licensing classes.

Most agents fail in that environment and start bouncing from broker to broker, picking up a few things along the way. The brokers who take this approach tend to suffer a lot of agent churn, earn little to no repeat business and face wild swings in revenue. It creates an unnecessary additional workload and cost, and becomes disastrous during slow market conditions when the volume of newly introduced agents declines.

Sources indicate that broker B, on the other hand, adopts a mentorship approach. They figure if they’re going to take the time to hire and onboard a newly introduced agent, they might as well give them everything they need to be as successful as possible.

Agents are more likely to thrive in this environment, and they get traction a lot faster too. As a result, they also tend to stick around longer, which means lower HR costs and more repeat business. It’s a win for you, your agents, and clients.

It has been revealed that the challenge is how to implement a system to effectively support your agents without breaking the bank. And the good news is it’s not as expensive or time consuming as you might think.

Rome wasn’t built in a day, and your support system won’t be either, so you’ll need to break it into three elements:.

Recent findings suggest that start small and simple. A well-rounded library of real estate books that align with your approach is the foundation of your training. You or your top agents can hold weekly classes teaching the material, followed by Q&A.

According to recent reports, then, begin developing your own training materials that are tailored to your business and market. Start by creating an outline of the topics you want agents to master, and then prioritize them by order of importance. Now start teaching classes on these topics, and after a few sessions, refine the material based on the questions your agents ask. Once it’s dialed in, you can record a perfect version, and only do the Q&A portion live. Over the course of a year, you should have a robust library of training videos.

Just be sure to keep it up to date as laws and regulations, industry and market statistics, and your internal processes change.

This is an area you probably shouldn’t create your own training material because it’s a unique expertise.

Sources indicate that you can start with the same foundational approach as with the technical training by teaching your agents based on trusted books from authoritative experts. Tony Robbins, Jocko Willink, Robert Greene, Gary John Bishop, and if you’re feeling particularly edgy, maybe even David Goggins, are all great options. And there are many interactive programs, both in-person and virtual, that you can send your agents to.

In a recent development, in full disclosure, I published a book on this topic titled “Unlock Your MVP”, but it was based on my own journey of building a brokerage producing over $2 billion in transactions, surviving three heart attacks, battling three NAR class action lawsuits, and then going on to build a fresh brokerage from scratch to over 1,100 agents in just nine months as its CEO and qualifying broker. So I have what most would consider a fairly unique perspective.

This is where it gets tougher because mentorship requires a sizable investment of time and energy.

The approach I’ve taken is to be the primary mentor. As those agents become more successful, other agents become more receptive to participating. And it’s easier to get your top producers to take an active role in mentoring agents if you incentivise them and frame it from the perspective of mentorship helping them to become more proficient themselves and opening opportunities to partner with their mentees for a commission split.

Growing your brokerage requires you to create an environment that enables your agents to become more successful more quickly. Most brokers never make this investment and they suffer as a result, so if you want to thrive, build an effective support system.

Derek Carlson is the president and managing broker of Realty ONE Group MVP, a Florida based real estate brokerage firm with over 1,100 Realtors.

UPDATED 07:16 EST / NOVEMBER 20 2026.

In a recent development, data center backlash is pushing builders to show communities what they get in return, and public-private partnerships are becoming one answer. As the race for sovereign AI heats up, the question is shifting from where intellectual property lives to where compute runs and who profits from it.

Canada offers a sharp test case. A modern data hall employs few people, but its profits can fund the startups and jobs a region needs, according to Sharif Virani (pictured), chief executive officer of SPUR Innovation Center.

“There’s a big misnomer right now in the world that’s kind of landing from previous tech, where people think where your IP is where the wealth creation is going to be,” he said. “It’s not the case anymore. You have to make sure your inference happens in your country or in your region.”.

Virani spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and host Rebecca Knight at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed sovereign AI, reinvesting data center profits in local entrepreneurs and winning over residents through public-private partnerships. (* Disclosure below.).

It has been revealed that SPUR treats its Waterloo, Ontario, site as an innovation campus with an attached data hall rather than a pure data center. The firm reinvests about 10 percent of the campus’s data center profits in local entrepreneurs through a venture studio and takes first right of refusal on their office space and compute, Virani explained. Canada’s Dominion List counts more than 500 founders who have left for San Francisco, he noted.

Industry observers note that “We have entrepreneurship at an all-time low, productivity at an all-time low [and] GDP in freefall,” he remarked. “That’s really the result. We’ve got to reverse that.”.

One of SPUR’s early investments went to two international students who had full scholarships to the University of Toronto and internships lined up in San Francisco. Instead, they launched a startup called Auditorium AI and hired staff, according to Virani. The model also reaches Main Street, where on-campus hackathons helped a former long-haul trucker build AI software for logistics.

“AI allows these people who know the problem, who have earned the right to solve the problem, to mobilize technology to do it and make the lives of their friends, families and neighbors better,” Virani noted.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After an crucial hackathon that demonstrated how AI agents could autonomously perform payments using blockchain, global payments giant Mastercard has spotlighted the XRP Ledger (XRPL).

36 hours. 179 hackers. 70 submissions. At the XRP Ledger Hackathon, developers used Mastercard Agent Pay for machines to explore new possibilities for micropayments and autonomous commerce, including how AI agents can transact within defined spending limits and with verified merchants. See what we learned about the future of agentic commerce: https://t.co/S4NwQxxuRi #AgenticCommerce #DigitalAssets #AI.

Industry observers note that global payments giant Mastercard recently posted on X about the outcome of the XRP Ledger Hackathon. In the post, the payments firm detailed that 179 developers submitted 70 projects during the 36-hour event in Manhattan.

The focus of the competition was how to enable AI-powered agents to autonomously execute transactions and micropayments, engage with verified merchants and so forth, all while operating within budgets set by developers.

The hackathon was held as part of the preparations for Ripple’s annual conference called Swell. Mastercard, Amazon Web Services, QuickNode and Ledger supported the event, which had a prize pool of over $40,000.

Mastercard published an official article in which it mentioned the challenge given to developers. They had to build AI agents that could autonomously make payments to verified merchants without human input.

In a recent development, also, the agents had to operate within a specified budget. They had to settle payments using Ripple’s USD-backed stablecoin called RLUSD. They had to do this on the XRP Ledger.

One of the purposes of the challenge was to showcase how blockchain infrastructure can enable micropayments. This is especially the case for micropayments smaller than one cent.

In the future, these micropayments could be valuable as AI agents start buying computational resources or requesting data from other AI agents and then making payments themselves for digital services.

Mastercard’s vice president of digital assets, Michael Broderick, stressed that the tech giant's technology called Agent Pay for Machines could enable such payments.

It has been revealed that the project that won the competition is called Wraps. Its creators are Adarsha Mishra and Hrishabh Ayush. Their project dealt with how to secure user privacy in AI-based transactions. Their project demonstrated a method to prove that search logs were not being saved.

One of the most interesting things mentioned in the Mastercard report might be how the XRP Ledger is increasingly being used for payments by machines.

Mastercard mentioned that over 500,000 transactions are being conducted daily on the XRPL by AI agents.

Also, it’s reported that Ripple has recorded over 10 million payments using the x402 internet payment protocol on XRPL. This comes less than three months after the protocol crossed the 1 million payment milestone on the network.

Exchange Ledgers in the Middle as CFTC and SEC Diverge on What “Delivery” Means

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1250 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • exchange and the app shows the balance.
  • It has been revealed that under the SEC's crypto proposal, delivery doesn't decide the question at all.
  • Recent findings suggest that open almost any crypto exchange app after a purchase and you'll see a clean number: 1.0000 ETH, available.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

A customer buys a token on a U.S. exchange and the app shows the balance. Under the CFTC's December 14 framework, nothing has been delivered yet.

It has been revealed that under the SEC's crypto proposal, delivery doesn't decide the question at all. An October 27 comment letter asks the two agencies to settle on one answer.

Recent findings suggest that open almost any crypto exchange app after a purchase and you'll see a clean number: 1.0000 ETH, available. To the customer, the asset is theirs. To the exchange's database, it's a row in an internal ledger. To federal regulators, that row is now being judged by two different tests that don't agree on what it means.

According to recent reports, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on what it calls Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions (CTX) and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (CAM). It sets out the agency's first formal view of "actual delivery" for crypto since it withdrew its 2020 guidance last December. Comments close on December 14.

Industry observers note that the Securities and Exchange Commission's Regulation Crypto Assets proposal takes a different view of the same moment. Then, on October 27, a comment letter on the SEC's file raised the gap directly. It described the situation as "two conflicting definitions of the same physical facts" and asked the agencies to "please coordinate the definitions.".

Delivery matters because it decides which rulebook applies.

For the CFTC, the answer comes from Section 2(c)(2)(D) of the Commodity Exchange Act. A leveraged, margined or financed retail commodity trade is treated like a futures contract unless "actual delivery" happens within 28 days. If delivery happens in time, the trade falls outside futures rules. If it doesn't, the exchange is effectively running a futures venue.

For the SEC, the question is whether a token is still part of an investment contract. Under the August proposal, a covered investment contract ends when the issuer has finished or permanently stopped its essential managerial efforts and files a Form TR transition report. Whether the buyer has received the token is not part of that test.

So one agency treats delivery as the deciding question, and the other barely considers it.

The CFTC's position is still preliminary, but it is detailed. Published in the Federal Register on October 13, the notice relies on the Monex case standard: actual delivery requires "the transfer of some meaningful degree of possession or control.".

For crypto, the agency suggests that possession and control "may require possession of the credentials (e.g., private key(s))." It takes three positions that matter most to exchanges:.

The agency is also asking whether control has to be exclusive, whether delivery can happen while a lien or security interest is outstanding, and how financing offered in an exchange's standard account documents affects whether a trade is covered at all.

In a recent development, the SEC's proposal, released on August 18, deals with a different question. It creates offering exemptions, including a $5 million startup exemption over four years, and a safe harbor for when a crypto asset's investment contract ends. Neither depends on where the token sits.

According to recent reports, under the proposal, a token held in a customer's self-custody wallet and a token recorded on an exchange's books are treated the same way. In both cases, the investment contract question depends on the issuer's managerial efforts and its filings.

That is the gap the October 27 letter tries to close. Its author, who describes themselves as a fintech founder designing a consumer platform, argues that "where the customer holds the private keys or execution is on-chain, with custody evidence, the asset should be treated as delivered and the covered-investment-contract analysis should end there.".

Running four common exchange transactions through both frameworks shows where the tests split.

Trade one: a fully paid purchase left on the exchange.

Trade two: the same purchase withdrawn to a self-custody wallet on day three.

Trade three: a margined purchase kept on the exchange's ledger for 30 days.

Trade four: an on-chain swap that settles directly into the user's wallet.

Industry observers note that the pattern is consistent. Self-custody is the only position that clearly counts as delivery under the CFTC's view and also ends the analysis under the letter's proposed SEC fix. Everything left on an exchange's internal ledger stays in an unclear position. The CFTC treats it as undelivered and the SEC's text doesn't address it.

The letter was filed on October 27, a week after the SEC's October 20 comment deadline. It is anonymous and brief, but its main concern is practical. If the definitions stay separate, it warns, founders will have to design products around whichever rule is stricter.

It is the only filing on either docket so far that sets the two definitions side by side.

The CFTC process is still at the advance-notice stage, so a formal proposal will follow. For U.S. platforms, though, the direction is clear. Under the CFTC's preliminary reading, an exchange that keeps customer assets in internal ledger accounts has not delivered them. If that exchange also offers margin or financing, it is on track to be treated as a futures venue.

According to recent reports, the SEC's final rule could adopt the letter's custody-based approach or keep delivery out of its analysis entirely. Until one of those happens, the same ledger entry can be undelivered for one regulator and irrelevant for the other.

Exchanges and their customers have until December 14 to say which definition should prevail. The real decision is whether "delivered" ends up meaning the same thing at both agencies.

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 17, 2026 at 3:00 amNovember 16, 2026 at 12:58 pm.

Fairly, a Portland, Ore.-based vacation rental startup led by Vacasa founder Eric Breon, raised a $22.4 million Series A round, the organization announced Tuesday.

Oregon Venture Fund led the round, with participation from Elevate Capital and Breon.

According to recent reports, fairly pairs vacation rental owners with local caretakers who look after the homes. Its software handles pricing, bookings and scheduling, and uses AI to draft routine guest messages and flag maintenance problems.

Industry observers note that guests booked more than $66 million in reservations through Fairly over the past year, up from about $5 million the year before, the tech giant noted. Nearly 900 caretakers now manage about 2,000 homes across 47 states, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

In a recent development, owners pay a single 20% fee, which Fairly splits with the caretaker, compared with the 25% to 40% the organization indicates other managers typically charge. Fairly also says it doesn’t tack extra fees onto guest bills, so guests pay less overall.

In a recent development, “At Vacasa, I led a 7,000-person team, and delivering quality, individualized care at that scale is not an easy task,” Breon remarked in a statement. “At Fairly, we take a completely different approach: we empower dedicated, hyperlocal caretakers to care for homes, and our systems do the heavy lifting around them.”.

Breon founded Vacasa in Portland in 2009 and spent more than a decade there. The tech giant went public via a SPAC deal in 2021 and was acquired in May 2025 by Phoenix-based Casago, a vacation rental manager.

Fairly, founded in 2023, emerged from stealth in December 2024 with $10.1 million in pre-seed funding. The organization has now raised $32.5 million in total.

According to recent reports, fairly now employs 106 people, up from 25 at its launch in 2024. Co-founder Subechya Person remains chief product officer; co-founder and former CTO Jeff Flitton left the company in February.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage applications for fresh-home purchases fell 13.6% year over year in October as rising mortgage rates and affordability pressures weighed on buyer demand, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association’s (MBA) Builder Application Survey.
  • Applications also declined 7% from September.
  • The 30-year fixed mortgage rate climbed about 60 basis points over the two months leading up to October, reaching 7.5% last month, said Joel Kan, MBA’s vice president and deputy chief economist.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage applications for fresh-home purchases fell 13.6% year over year in October as rising mortgage rates and affordability pressures weighed on buyer demand, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association’s (MBA) Builder Application Survey.

Applications also declined 7% from September. The figures are not adjusted for seasonal patterns.

The 30-year fixed mortgage rate climbed about 60 basis points over the two months leading up to October, reaching 7.5% last month, said Joel Kan, MBA’s vice president and deputy chief economist.

“As a result, applications for the purchase of newly built homes declined year-over-year for the fourth consecutive month,” Kan remarked.

MBA’s estimate of latest-home sales increased slightly in October, but the annualized sales pace for the past two months remained at its weakest level since July 2022. Affordability pressures and uncertainty surrounding mortgage rates have prompted prospective buyers to delay purchases, even as builders continue offering incentives, Kan remarked.

MBA estimated that fresh single-family home sales ran at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 592,000 units in October, up 1.4% from September’s pace of 584,000 units.

On an unadjusted basis, MBA estimated 44,000 latest-home sales in October, down 6.4% from 47,000 in September.

Recent findings suggest that conventional loans accounted for 47.9% of upcoming-home mortgage applications in October, while Federal Housing Administration (FHA) loans made up 36.9%. U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) loans accounted for 14.1%, and  U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) loans represented 1%.

The average loan size for new homes declined to $368,934 in October from $374,724 in September.

In a recent development, MBA’s Builder Application Survey tracks mortgage application volume from homebuilder-affiliated mortgage companies nationwide. The association uses the data, along with other market information and assumptions, to estimate latest-home sales at the national, state and metropolitan levels.

The survey provides an early indication of new-home sales because mortgage applications typically coincide with contract signings, when the Census Bureau records new-home sales in its monthly report.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has opened historic doors for blockchain technology adoption in traditional financial markets as it approves exchange and clearinghouse applications for blockchain-based derivatives market infrastructure.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 16, CFTC Chairman Michael Selig announced that the commission had given the green light to exchange (designated contract market or DCM) and clearinghouse (derivatives clearing organization or DCO) applications for a manufacturer using blockchain technology for the execution and settlement of derivatives contracts.

As per the official statement, Selig considers this a major step forward for U.S. financial markets. He said that blockchain-based market infrastructure is compatible with current U.S. financial regulations.

"This approval makes clear that there is a regulatory path for companies that want to innovate and use blockchain technology to modernize how derivatives are traded and settled,"  he elaborated.

Recent findings suggest that selig pointed out that the U.S. derivatives markets have seen a number of technological advancements, from physical trading floors to electronic trading platforms.

Now, with blockchain technology, he believes there is an opportunity to further modernize financial market infrastructure without losing regulatory oversight and investor protections.

Notably, there is no technical architecture requirement imposed on derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses under the CFTC's current regulatory framework.

Therefore, firms that leverage blockchain-based networks can apply for regulatory approval under the same set of rules and regulations that apply to traditional financial market participants.

However, Selig also clarified that blockchain adoption is not a license to escape regulatory oversight.

Companies will still need to comply with rules covering anti-money laundering (AML), client protections, market monitoring, risk mitigation and other measures designed to protect the integrity of financial markets.

Simply put, the CFTC is looking to bring blockchain technology into regulated derivatives market infrastructure while maintaining the same standards as traditional financial market participants.

Recent findings suggest that for some time, the CFTC chairman has been pushing for a scenario where U.S. companies developing emerging financial technologies can operate in the country without having to look to international markets.

The latest developments further reinforce the message that the U.S. is open for business for companies building blockchain-based financial market infrastructure, according to Selig.

Radian Aerospace plans to make its own composite materials for space plane (and for other companies, too)

💡 Key Takeaways

  • On the way to building a space plane, Seattle-based Radian Aerospace is planning a factory to make the advanced materials it’ll need — and it plans to sell those materials to other companies as well.
  • Radian CEO Richard Humphrey noted he envisions the factory, known as Foundry 1, as a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility with a footprint spanning “just under 100,000 square feet.” Six to 12 sites around the country — including sites in the Pacific Northwest — are presently under consideration, with late 2027 as the target for starting production, he said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Alan Boyle on Nov 17, 2026 at 4:00 amNovember 17, 2026 at 4:11 am.

On the way to building a space plane, Seattle-based Radian Aerospace is planning a factory to make the advanced materials it’ll need — and it plans to sell those materials to other companies as well.

Radian CEO Richard Humphrey noted he envisions the factory, known as Foundry 1, as a state-of-the-art manufacturing facility with a footprint spanning “just under 100,000 square feet.” Six to 12 sites around the country — including sites in the Pacific Northwest — are presently under consideration, with late 2027 as the target for starting production, he said.

Foundry 1 is meant to produce ceramic matrix composites, or CMCs — not only for Radian’s space plane, but also for other applications ranging from gas-turbine components to high-performance braking systems.

“Each of these industries has a bottleneck that’s being driven by a lack of an industrial base to really build these next-gen materials,” Humphrey told GeekWire.

Humphrey and his teammates ran into that bottleneck while developing Radian One, a reusable rocket-powered plane that’s meant to transport cargo and crew to and from low Earth orbit. Securing a reliable supply chain for the required materials proved so challenging that Radian decided to produce its own.

According to recent reports, “Defense and space programs need these materials at costs and production rates that today’s supply base cannot deliver,” Humphrey said today in a news release. “Foundry 1 unlocks a substantial commercial opportunity for Radian and a more direct path to revenue. It positions us to supply customers across these industries while advancing the technology that will make Radian One possible.”.

Industry observers note that ceramic matrix composites embed reinforcing fibers, such as carbon or silicon carbide, within a lightweight ceramic material. The ceramic provides resistance to extreme heat, while the fibers help the material carry loads and resist damage from cracking.

Carbon-fiber composites have been around for decades, but turning them into products is typically labor-intensive and expensive. To drive down the cost while improving quality, Radian is developing an automated system for producing CMCs. The organization indicates it’s targeting a 50% reduction in CMC manufacturing costs by cutting manual labor, shortening processing cycles and minimizing waste.

Sources indicate that artificial intelligence will play a role as well, Humphrey said. “We see an AI-native base where we can actually learn from each individual piece while digital-twinning them, so each piece ends up with a digital passport,” he said. “We know exactly where every fiber is, the angle of each fiber to the fiber next to it, and then we do in-process CT screening.”.

Industry observers note that greg Scofield, an adviser to Radian and former director of the Purdue Hypersonics Laboratory, said Radian is taking an integrated approach to the challenges surrounding CMC production. “Designing fiber placement, thermal processing and inspection together creates an opportunity to improve cost and quality throughout the production line, with benefits for customers across defense and space,” he said.

The payoff could be huge: A report from Polaris Market Research suggests the global market for advanced composites could rise to $126 billion by 2034.

In partnership with NASA’s Glenn Research Center, Radian has already tested a patent-pending composite material called Dur-E-Therm at temperatures exceeding 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit (1,480 degrees Celsius) under conditions that simulate hypersonic flight.

Radian’s next steps are to select the site for Foundry 1 and begin construction while continuing CMC development at partner facilities. That’s a tall order for a small organization.

Humphrey said the manufacturer at the moment has about 20 employees working at locations including the University of Washington’s Advanced Composites Center. Back in 2022, Radian declared a $27.5 million funding round that brought total investment to $32 million at the time. Humphrey said Radian has raised additional funding since then, but he wasn’t ready to share updated figures.

So, how much will Foundry 1 cost? “We’re not quite ready to put a pin in the number,” Humphrey noted. “It’s fair to say it’s sub — not a lot less, but it’s sub $100 million in terms of total capital to stand this up for what we’re doing.”.

It has been revealed that he acknowledged that following through on the plan for Foundry 1 will require raising more capital. “It is part of what we do, and we have a really super group of investors that have been behind us for a long time,” he mentioned.

Humphrey stated the Radian One space plane remains the focus of the manufacturer’s long-term vision — but for now, the company is devoting all of its resources and capital to Foundry 1.

Industry observers note that “It’s the bottleneck to Radian One being successful,” he said. “We think that by applying all of our attention to that, it serves the broader market but also serves advancing Radian One. Both of those are hard things, so we’re going to focus on one hard thing at a time.”.

Is Radian becoming an advanced materials and aerospace firm? Humphrey said that’s “a good way to think about it,” but he emphasized that aerospace still gets top billing.

“I’d rather be launching today than just be building CMCs,” he mentioned. “But building CMCs is what gets us to flying tomorrow. By advancing materials, it’s our single best way to be ready for Space 3.0, if you want to call it that. … At times we have to be adaptable to really move the project forward, and sometimes it goes a little sideways before you go forward. It’s just the way I’ve come to accept it.”.

Tracy, who has held several leadership roles at the credit union, including chief financial officer, currently oversees its retail, lending, technology, marketing and finance teams, while Moody is stepping down after 20 years as CEO.

NEXA Lending added Michael Lindsay, a military veteran and mortgage originator who funded more than $100 million in loans in 2025, with approximately 98% to 99% of his production coming from VA lending.

The Mortgage Bankers Association promoted Justin Wiseman to senior vice president of housing finance policy and general counsel, expanding his responsibilities to include oversight of the trade group’s legal affairs while continuing to lead its housing finance policy work.

Wiseman, who joined MBA in 2012 and most recently served as vice president and managing regulatory counsel, will also join the association’s Senior Management Team and oversee legal risk management, compliance and board governance.

First Horizon Bank named Andrew Finkle market president for Palm Beach and Broward counties in Florida, where he will lead the local team and oversee client relationships.

Finkle joined the bank in 2016 and previously served as commercial banking team lead for the two counties; he has more than 25 years of commercial and investment banking experience and five years of experience as a middle-market manufacturer’s chief financial officer.

Better Home & Finance Holding Manufacturer added two mortgage advisors to NEO Home Loans, expanding its presence in Southern California and along the Central Coast.

Brandon Goldberg, who leads Your Home Loan Surgeons in the San Diego area, and Lompoc-based Ryan Davis brought a combined $50 million in loan volume in 2025, with both specializing in purchase lending and local relationships with real estate agents and homebuilders.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Malicious JavaScript code snippets were planted on the websites of 178 organizations.

The exploit originated inside Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform, a tool that many large companies use for A/B testing, which means showing users multiple versions of a page to determine which one is more effective.

Report URI estimates that on November 16 the code sat in 188 of the 1,611 Optimizely snippets it crawled, and the real number is most likely higher.

Among the websites that could become victims of the hack are some of the largest names in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Fox News, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock. BleepingComputer confirms that the script loads on many of them.

It has been revealed that essentially, the script's goal was to swap a wallet address on the page for the attacker's one, capture card numbers, take screenshots of pages and more. It was a whole stack of tools used to steal personal data, wallets and other assets.

Sources indicate that according to Report URI, the attacker's wallets received about $7,040 within the first nine hours. That is a drop in the ocean considering the names involved, though the losses from card skimming are unknown. A card skimmer was added later that day, and a hidden iframe tried to load an iOS exploit chain on older iPhones.

Optimizely confirmed that an unauthorized party had exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation to add malicious JavaScript to certain customer projects. How the flaw worked is yet to be confirmed.

According to recent reports, if successful, it could become one of the largest supply-chain attacks we have ever witnessed. Considering the attack came from a third party, we might see one of the largest service migrations in the world, as none of the third-party services and libraries can be trusted nowadays if used through an API.

Cryptocurrency services delegate certain tasks to third-party providers all the time, so witnessing a similar situation in our field is more than a possibility.

According to recent reports, for product owners: stay cautious and rethink the use of services prone to exploits. For owners: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former National Association of Realtors Chief Financial Officer John Pierpoint has sued the organization for unpaid retirement compensation totaling more than $541,000, according to a complaint filed on Tuesday.

According to recent reports, pierpoint alleged NAR has paid senior vice presidents one year of their base salary at retirement since 2005. To avoid booking the full expense when a senior vice president retired, NAR created a Compensation Reserve that let it steadily set aside funds throughout the executive’s tenure, which it would release at retirement. Pierpoint helped establish the reserve in 2005 at the direction of former NAR CEO Dale Stinton, court documents noted.

Pierpoint retired from NAR on March 31, 2025 — a date he chose with the 2023 Sitzer | Burnett buyer-broker commission lawsuit in mind. The former CFO noted he was key in executing the buyer-broker commission settlement payout, which totaled $418 million. The first settlement payment, totaling roughly $200 million, was issued in February 2025, with subsequent payments of $72 million per year until the full $418 million is paid.

Industry observers note that pierpoint said he notified NAR of his impending retirement in late 2024 and requested his retirement payout. However, six days before his last day with NAR, Pierpoint alleged that a Grant Thornton auditor named White — there is no first name listed in the court documents — emailed him and said that “NAR had been ‘unable to locate any policy or verify any consistent practice’ concerning the Compensation Reserve or ‘the payout to executives of a full year of salary upon retirement.'”.

According to recent reports, white also allegedly said that the Compensation Reserve “was not used to fund” the exit packages of eight other senior vice presidents who retired before Pierpoint, which are listed in the court documents as L.J., F.S., B.M., D.H., J.G.,  J.B., D.G. and B.G. Real Estate News said L.J., D.G. and B.G. are likely former general counsel Laurie Janik, former SVP of talent development and resources Donna Gland, and former senior vice president and CEO Bob Goldberg.

As a result, Grant Thornton mentioned it was “unable to approve the payout of a full year’s compensation without any concrete proof that such act is mandated by an employment agreement, policy or plan.”.

Pierpoint claimed NAR had the funds to pay his retirement benefit and provided a ledger outlining what the Association allegedly reserved from December 2014 to December 2024. He also remarked the trial balances NAR provided to outside auditors, including Grant Thornton, included evidence of the Compensation Reserve’s existence and purpose.

“NAR carried its obligation to Pierpoint at approximately 97.6 cents on the dollar three months before it refused to pay him anything,” the complaint read. “The practice NAR now claims it cannot verify is documented in NAR’s own ledger, its own year-end schedules, its own payroll records and its own audit files, and was paid to every one of Pierpoint’s predecessors who retired. NAR did not stop believing in its obligation; it stopped wanting to pay it.”.

Visualized with the help of AI.

Pierpoint’s counsel accused NAR of shirking its obligation to pay the former CFO due to its financial woes after the settlement. In December 2025, former NAR president Kevin Sears remarked the buyer-broker commission settlement saved the Association’s finances — the other option was to file an appeal and declare bankruptcy.

“John Pierpoint helped guide NAR through an extraordinarily challenging period in its history, including the financial consequences of the antitrust litigation,” said David Fish, an attorney with Workplace Law Partners, P.C., who represents Pierpoint. “After nearly four decades of service, he expected the organization to honor the same retirement compensation practice it had followed for other senior executives.”.

“We believe the evidence will establish that the financial pressures following the antitrust verdict did not relieve NAR of its obligation to pay compensation earned by its employees,” he added.

Pierpoint’s counsel is requesting that NAR pay the $541,059 retirement payout, statutory damages of 5 percent of the unpaid amount for each month it remains unpaid, attorneys’ fees and costs, and prejudgment and post-judgment interest. They also seek a jury trial.

NAR denied Pierpoint’s claims, saying that the former CFO has “[mischaracterized] a varied set of individual arrangements with departing executives as a uniform and guaranteed retirement benefit.”.

According to recent reports, “Mr. Pierpoint was not entitled to the payment he now seeks, and NAR’s decision was unrelated to its antitrust settlement or its financial condition,” an NAR spokesperson told Inman in an emailed statement. “NAR is committed to appropriate financial controls and responsible stewardship of its members’ dues dollars. NAR pays compensation and benefits that are actually owed, not just because a former executive requests payment. No such obligation exists here, and we intend to vigorously defend against these claims through the appropriate legal process.”.

Clock Ticking on Zcash’s Sprout Pool: 22,263 ZEC Unmoved Ahead of NU7 Lock

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1212 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nulltx

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Daily pool data indicates Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped.
  • Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.
  • Sources indicate that most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Daily pool data indicates Sprout holders moved more than 300 ZEC out in a September rush, then almost stopped. The last withdrawal was on October 19.

Unless someone acts in the next few days, nearly all of what remains will be unspendable at block 3,543,405.

Sources indicate that most coverage of Zcash's upcoming Sprout freeze quotes the same figure, about 22,000 ZEC. That number is accurate, but it is a single snapshot. It doesn't show whether the people who own those coins are doing anything about the deadline.

We checked the pool every day, and the answer so far is no.

According to ZecStats' daily value-pool records, Sprout has held exactly 22,263.34162335 ZEC since October 19. That is 11 straight days, and more than 12,000 blocks, without a single zatoshi leaving the pool. Our October 25 piece recorded the drop from 22,309 ZEC to 22,263 ZEC. Since then the balance hasn't moved.

ZecStats publishes a daily CSV of every Zcash value pool, using the last block of each UTC day. Its figures follow the valuePools field that a full node returns through the getblockchaininfo call. The archive starts on July 30, 2026, and gives a 92-day picture of the Sprout pool.

According to recent reports, across those 92 days, about 374 ZEC, or 1.65% of the pool, left Sprout. That is an average of roughly 4 ZEC a day. The average hides the real pattern, though: the pool moved on only 15 of the 92 days.

Most of the withdrawals came in a few large transfers in September:.

Together with smaller moves on August 31, September 17 and September 19, the 30 days to September 29 saw 310.5 ZEC leave Sprout. That is about 10 ZEC a day.

October was much quieter. Apart from one withdrawal of 46.05 ZEC on October 19, the month's activity was small change:.

Since October 19, there has been no movement at all.

In a recent development, at September's pace, about 70 ZEC more would leave before activation. At October's pace, it would be well under 15 ZEC. On the last 11 days' pace, the answer is zero.

Recent findings suggest that the deadline is set in ZIP 259, which defines how the NU7 network upgrade is deployed. It sets the mainnet activation height at 3,543,405.

NU7 does not introduce a newly introduced transaction format. Instead, after activation, version 4 transactions become invalid, while versions 5 and 6 remain valid. Sprout's design is the problem. As ZIP 259 puts it: "Because Sprout transfers can only be represented by version 4 transactions, funds remaining in the Sprout pool become unspendable.".

Industry observers note that the coins would not be destroyed, and NU7 does not change Zcash's supply cap. They would simply be stuck in a pool that no valid transaction can spend from. Today the stranded amount would be 22,263 ZEC, about 0.13% of the roughly 17.01 million ZEC in circulation.

The rest of the upgrade is larger:.

It has been revealed that ZIP 259 also skips Zcash's usual three-month gap between the first supporting software release and activation. Operators running unsupported software could stay online and follow a pre-NU7 chain.

Recent findings suggest that as of ZecStats' latest upgrade on October 30 at 13:09 UTC, the chain was at block 3,535,877. That leaves 7,528 blocks until activation.

Recent findings suggest that in October, the network averaged about 1,147 blocks a day, or one roughly every 75.3 seconds. At that rate, block 3,543,405 arrives around 02:00–03:00 UTC on November 6. That is the evening of November 5 in the Americas and the early hours of November 6 in Europe and Africa.

Small changes in block times could move that window by a few hours. Holders who blueprint to move funds on the final day risk missing the cutoff.

In a recent development, in practice, getting funds out of Sprout means sending a version 4 transaction that moves them into a newer pool before activation. Owners need software that can still build Sprout transactions and a synced node or wallet that recognizes their old notes.

Sources indicate that the September withdrawals show that some holders are still paying attention. Several were round amounts, such as 99.998 ZEC, which is consistent with someone moving 100 ZEC and paying a fee. The 11-day pause since October 19 suggests something else: most of the remaining 22,263 ZEC may belong to keys that are lost, forgotten or no longer used.

That has been part of the debate about Sprout for years. A pool that has been shrinking slowly since Zcash's early days is now on a fixed timetable. The daily data indicates that most of its remaining balance is not being moved.

Recent findings suggest that every report that cites "about 22,000 ZEC at risk" is technically correct. The more useful figure for anyone tracking the upgrade is the rate of change, and right now that rate is zero.

According to recent reports, the useful thing to watch over the next week is whether the Sprout line in ZecStats' daily data moves again before block 3,543,405. If it doesn't, Zcash will activate NU7 with about 22,263 ZEC permanently locked in its first shielded pool. That would be one of the largest deliberate freezes of user funds by any major blockchain upgrade, and nearly all of it would be coins whose owners did not move them in time.

MIAMI, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sanctuary Wealth ("Sanctuary"), a leading platform that provides elite financial advisors the freedom, flexibility, control and choice to thrive in an evolving industry, today confirmed that existing investor Kennedy Lewis Investment Management ("Kennedy Lewis") has committed $250 million in latest growth capital to the firm.

The investment will allow Sanctuary to broaden the expertise its Partner Firms can draw on to serve clients more comprehensively, attract new business and pursue acquisitions. It will also give Sanctuary greater flexibility to provide capital when Partner Firm owners want to finance growth, monetize a portion of their equity or prepare for succession.

Recent findings suggest that "Sanctuary's platform was built to help wirehouse advisors become independent, deepen relationships with their clients and build enterprise value in firms of their own. That heritage remains central to Sanctuary's identity and growth strategy," mentioned Adam Malamed, Chief Executive Officer of Sanctuary Wealth. "As our Partner Firms continue to evolve, this newly introduced capital enhances our ability to invest in what they need as established businesses, giving them more ways to grow and their owners more options for realizing the value they have created.".

Industry observers note that the depth and breadth of the platform Sanctuary has developed over the past eight years has attracted increasing interest from advisors and independent wealth management firms across the industry. In response, the firm has added affiliation options to give the industry's most sophisticated advisors more choice and flexibility to pursue their vision and objectives.

Industry observers note that "Our Partner Firms are our clients, and we have to earn their business every day," mentioned Vince Fertitta and Robert Walter, Co-Presidents of Sanctuary Wealth. "After years of helping advisors build enterprise value in their firms, we want them to have more ways to put that value to work. Founders should be able to monetize their businesses on their own timeline by selling a minority or majority stake and keep leading the business on the same independent terms that made ownership so attractive to them in the first place.".

Sanctuary's network now includes 125 Partner Firms, with $71 billion in assets on the platform or in transition. To date, Sanctuary has made 13 minority investments in its Partner Firms.

Industry observers note that building on a partnership established in 2022The $250 million commitment from Kennedy Lewis, a multi-strategy private credit manager with approximately $40 billion in assets under management, consists of $50 million in mandatory convertible debt and a $200 million delayed-draw term loan. Kennedy Lewis has also elected to convert its existing outstanding convertible debt investment in Sanctuary into equity.

Sources indicate that "Our partnership with Sanctuary demonstrates what can be accomplished when a talented leadership team and a committed capital partner share a common vision," said David Chene, Co-Founder of Kennedy Lewis. "We have tremendous confidence in Adam and his team, who have overseen growth that includes doubling the number of Partner Firms and almost tripling the assets on the platform since our initial investment in 2022. We believe Sanctuary is uniquely positioned to help independent advisors build and grow valuable businesses and are excited to deepen our partnership to support this next chapter.".

It has been revealed that "Sanctuary carefully considered the best path forward for this upcoming phase of our evolution and chose to expand our relationship with Kennedy Lewis," continued Malamed. "Kennedy Lewis understands our business and is completely aligned with our focus on helping our Partner Firms achieve their full potential. We look forward to continuing this constructive relationship and working together to capture Sanctuary's long-term opportunity.".

The transaction follows a thorough evaluation and negotiation of financing proposals by a dedicated committee of Sanctuary's Board. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to customary closing conditions, including the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the Hart Scott Rodino Act and FINRA approval.

Goldman Sachs served as exclusive financial advisor to Sanctuary in connection with the transaction, and Willkie Farr & Gallagher LLP served as legal advisor. Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld LLP served as legal advisor to Kennedy Lewis.

About Sanctuary WealthSanctuary is a leading hybrid RIA that provides comprehensive wealth management solutions and platform partnerships to sophisticated independent wealth management firms.

Through its Partnered Independence model, Sanctuary helps advisors seeking greater freedom, flexibility, control and choice transition from large financial institutions to build enduring businesses of their own.

Sanctuary Wealth was built to serve elite wirehouse breakaway advisors. Today, Sanctuary supports a growing community of Partner Firms across a range of business models with integrated technology, marketing, operations and a robust, open-architecture platform, enabling advisors to serve clients at the highest level while building long-term enterprise value.

  • Vayo, the Seattle-based AI travel startup launched by Booking Holdings last month, is expanding beyond its initial focus on tracking travel plans — starting to use AI agents to book flights, hotels, rental cars and activities on behalf of owners in its invite-only beta.
  • Industry observers note that that includes bookings on Expedia, the flagship site of Booking Holdings’ biggest rival, Expedia Group.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

by Todd Bishop on Nov 17, 2026 at 6:20 amNovember 17, 2026 at 6:21 am.

Vayo, the Seattle-based AI travel startup launched by Booking Holdings last month, is expanding beyond its initial focus on tracking travel plans — starting to use AI agents to book flights, hotels, rental cars and activities on behalf of owners in its invite-only beta.

Industry observers note that that includes bookings on Expedia, the flagship site of Booking Holdings’ biggest rival, Expedia Group. Vayo confirmed that its AI agents book there by navigating Expedia’s website, without a direct integration or partnership for those bookings.

The firm notes Vayo recommends the best option for the traveler, wherever that option is booked, not just through its parent company’s brands.

According to recent reports, vayo is led by Mike Fridgen, a longtime Seattle entrepreneur with deep roots in travel. Booking Holdings, the parent of Booking.com, Priceline, Kayak and OpenTable, noted last month that it plans to invest $100 million in Vayo, depending on its progress and market conditions.

Companies are still working out how to handle AI agents that use their sites on behalf of customers. In September, Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agent from shopping on Amazon.com, saying the agent didn’t identify itself.

Recent findings suggest that when Vayo launched last month, Fridgen said it was relying on APIs and direct partnerships with travel companies, in part to avoid the risk of being blocked. Vayo notes no site has blocked its bookings so far.

How the bookings work: Vayo’s latest booking features work in two ways. It can book hotels, rental cars and activities through a direct connection with sister firm Booking.com, and it has similar links to OpenTable for restaurants and SeatGeek for event tickets.

For flights and other bookings, its AI agents navigate the booking websites, signing in to the traveler’s existing accounts where needed and completing the purchase. Every booking requires the traveler’s approval, the firm indicates.

If a site doesn’t allow AI agents, Vayo leaves that booking to the traveler.

According to recent reports, vayo uses 1Password to sign in to travelers’ accounts and, on sites other than Booking.com, Stripe’s Link agent wallet to pay, without seeing their passwords or card details, the firm states. It reports a reservation as confirmed only after the supplier confirms it.

Sources indicate that payments and pricing: Travelers pay whichever company they book with, and Vayo is not the merchant of record. The company declined to share details on commissions, saying its partner arrangements are still taking shape and won’t factor into its recommendations.

When Booking.com has the best option, Vayo users get Genius Level 3 pricing, Booking.com’s top loyalty tier, with discounts of up to 20% on select stays.

Recent findings suggest that the service is free to use during the invite-only beta. Responding to GeekWire’s questions, Vayo didn’t say how many people are using it or how many have completed a booking.

Who’s behind Vayo: Fridgen, the Vayo co-founder and CEO, was on the founding team of Expedia’s vacation-package business, led Alaska Airlines’ digital business and was founding head of product at airfare-prediction startup Farecast, before leading Decide.com and Madrona Venture Labs.

His co-founder and CTO is Allen Chen, the former CTO of Fanatics Collectibles, who previously co-founded Seattle software startups CloudPress and DataBlade. Ian Fliflet, OfferUp’s former chief growth officer, is head of growth. Vayo had about 20 employees, all working in downtown Seattle, when it released last month.

Next on its product roadmap, the tech giant says it looks to work inside the messaging apps people already use, and to let groups of travelers proposal trips together.

In a recent development, according to House of Stake, the reduction will start one quarter after ratification, and validators still have to adopt the protocol upgrade. The issuance cap will reach 1.6% after 24 months.

Ternullo estimated in HSP-029 that NEAR will avoid issuing 11.8 million tokens over two years. At the current price, these tokens would be worth around $38.5 million.

According to recent reports, the proposal also calculated that the staking yield of NEAR will go down from around 5.27% to around 3.37% if the staking ratio stays the same. More than half of all NEAR is not staked, according to House of Stake.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

Burn limits on Circle's legacy USDC bridge began falling on October 31, and the V1 contracts pause on December 1.

On the same migration page, a block of instructions written for AI coding assistants still says Noble, Sui and Aptos "still require V1." Circle's own release notes say two of those three chains moved to V2 weeks ago.

Industry observers note that circle's legacy cross-chain transfer protocol entered its final month today. From October 31, burn limits on CCTP V1 start falling toward zero, and on December 1 the V1 contracts pause. Any app still using them will stop moving USDC between chains.

According to recent reports, most coverage has focused on those two dates. But the guide developers are told to follow, Circle's V1-to-V2 migration page, contains a mistake in the section written for AI tools.

Industry observers note that embedded in the page is an "Agent Instructions" block, guidance meant for AI coding assistants that read the documentation for developers. It states: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1." For two of those three chains, Circle's other published records say the opposite.

The schedule is fixed. Circle announced in an August 27 blog post that "CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation begins October 31, 2026 and completes on December 1, 2026.".

From today, V1 burn limits fall, and the migration guide claims "message limits will tighten over time until no newly introduced burns can be initiated." On December 1 the V1 contracts pause, and any integration still pointing at them can no longer transfer USDC between chains.

Industry observers note that circle has been firm about this. "Migration from CCTP V1 (Legacy) to CCTP V2 is required, not just recommended," the company wrote, adding that V2 "uses separate contracts and APIs and is not backward compatible.".

Recent findings suggest that funds already in transit are protected. The guide says "all pending redemptions will remain available" during the phase-out, and that Circle "will maintain minter allowances greater than the total of pending attestations.".

The migration page has two audiences. Human readers see the main guide. AI coding assistants also parse a separate instruction block, which tells them how to answer developer questions.

In that block, the guidance is clear: "Noble, Sui, and Aptos still require V1.".

The main text above it says something different. According to the human-facing guide, "CCTP V2 contracts are available on all CCTP V1 chains except for Noble and Sui," and "Sui will be supported by V2 before the deprecation begins." Aptos isn't listed as an exception there at all.

So one page gives two different answers about the same chains, and the out-of-date answer is the one written for AI tools.

Circle's 2026 CCTP release notes show how out of date the instruction is:.

Circle's supported chains and domains page now lists both Sui and Aptos in its CCTP table, with Standard Transfer support. The page's V1-only section names one chain: Noble.

Sources indicate that as of today, Aptos has had V2 for more than two months and Sui for more than three weeks. The instruction telling AI tools that both "still require V1" was overtaken by Circle's own updates before the shutdown began.

Noble is the one chain in that line where the instruction is still accurate, and it is leaving CCTP entirely.

In a September 10 announcement, Circle said "Noble will not receive CCTP V2" and set out its exit:.

For Noble, V1 is the only route available, and it is being closed.

A wrong line in documentation would normally be a small issue, but the timing makes this one more serious.

Many developers now ask AI assistants to write or update integration code, and those assistants read documentation like this page. A developer asking how to bridge USDC to Sui or Aptos could be told, based on Circle's own instruction block, to use V1. That is the route whose burn limits started falling today and which pauses in a month.

The fix in the code is not small either. Moving to V2 means:.

An integration built on V1 now would have to be rebuilt within weeks.

For teams working with Sui and Aptos, the published records point one way: build on V2, using the contract addresses for domains 8 and 9. Don't follow the V1 guidance from the agent-instruction block.

In a recent development, for Noble, the deadline is January 12, 2027. Before then, integrators need to remove Noble as a CCTP route, and holders need to move or redeem their USDC.

Sources indicate that for everyone else, the burn-limit reductions have started. December 1 is the last day V1 integrations work, and any app still on V1 after that will stop moving USDC between chains.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that luxury real estate trends, changing homebuyer preferences and brokerage expansion are among the latest developments across the industry. This roundup also highlights top-producing agents, an association leadership change and a Central Florida brokerage joining a national platform while retaining its independence.

The Agency has released its 2027 Red Paper, examining the wealth dynamics, buyer preferences and design innovations shaping luxury real estate markets worldwide.

Drawing on insights from its global network of agents and industry leaders, the report identifies trends expected to influence luxury real estate in 2027.

In a recent development, “The global luxury real estate market is moving in more than one direction at once,” said Mauricio Umansky, CEO and founder of RealTrends Verified brokerage The Agency. Read the Red Paper report.

Affordability pressures are changing how Americans think about homeownership, with buyers prioritizing flexible living spaces, personal expression and long-term functionality, according to the 2027 Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate Trends Report.

The report identifies three trends: distinctive design, creative uses for existing space and longer-term homeownership.

Industry observers note that buyers are embracing color. More than half of respondents (55%) noted distinctive color choices would make them more likely to purchase a home. Younger buyers were particularly receptive, with 79% of Gen Z respondents and 64% of millennials favoring distinctive colors, compared with 38% of baby boomers and older consumers.

Homeowners are maximizing existing space. With higher housing costs making moves and additions less practical, 53% said they had repurposed underused space within the past one to three years. Another 72% blueprint to optimize unused areas in the coming year. Common conversions include home offices, storage, fitness areas and guest accommodations. Additionally, 81% said outdoor amenities could influence their choice between similarly priced homes.

It has been revealed that buyers are thinking longer term. Consumers are considering how homes can accommodate multiple life stages. Nearly one-third (31%) would accept an older home needing updates, while 30% would compromise on square footage.

Nearly half (47%) favor smaller improvements over time, compared with 26% who prefer major renovations.

The findings suggest affordability challenges are shifting consumer priorities toward adaptability, comfort and long-term livability.

Trifecta Real Estate, a locally owned brokerage in Brandon, Mississippi, has affiliated with Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate (BHGRE).

Now operating as Better Homes and Gardens Real Estate Trifecta, the firm was founded in 2023 by brokers Tye Densford and Alex Alexander.

Densford brings 20 years of experience as an agent, developer and former homebuilder. Alexander also has a homebuilding background and more than a decade of experience as an insurance agent.

Three Summit Sotheby’s International Realty RealTrends Verified agents — Sheila Hall, Michael LaPay and Chris Maddox — have been named among Sotheby’s International Realty’s Top 100 agents worldwide.

The distinction recognizes agents based on annual sales volume across a global network of more than 26,000 associates in 1,100 offices across 86 countries and territories.

Hall, earning her fourth Top 100 recognition, serves as director of real estate sales and exclusive listing agent for Deer Valley East Village, the first upcoming alpine village developed in the United States in more than 40 years.

LaPay, a five-time honoree, has more than four decades of Park City real estate experience and has ranked as Summit Sotheby’s top-producing agent since 2016.

Maddox brings nearly 20 years of experience, including 13 in greater Park City, specializing in master-planned golf communities and luxury properties.

Canopy Realtor Association has appointed Rob Nanfelt as its next CEO, effective Jan. 4, 2027. He succeeds Anne Marie DeCatsye, who is retiring after 26 years of leadership. Nanfelt will also serve as CEO of Canopy Housing Foundation.

Nanfelt brings more than 25 years of experience in executive leadership, association management, strategic planning, government affairs and public policy.

As executive director of the Real Estate & Building Industry Coalition (REBIC), he has worked with business executives, elected officials and community leaders on economic development, infrastructure and transportation initiatives in the Charlotte region.

Lively Real Estate has joined RealTrends Verified ENRG Realty as an independent brand, allowing the Central Florida boutique brokerage to retain its identity and leadership while gaining access to ENRG’s national platform.

Gernelle and Dan Bokuniewicz will continue to own and lead Lively, with expanded operational support, national resources and revenue-sharing opportunities for agents.

“For a change to be worth it, Dan and I needed full ownership of Lively and the freedom to shape its future. We had worked hard to build a brand our community knows and trusts, so any move had to support that vision. It also had to offer meaningful opportunities for our agents, support for their businesses, and additional ways to build long-term income,” mentioned Gernelle Bokuniewicz, founder of Lively Real Estate.

ERA Property Elite expands into Morgantown with KLM Properties acquisition.

ERA Property Elite, based in Charleston, West Virginia, has acquired KLM Properties Inc., expanding its reach into Morgantown and North Central West Virginia.

Founded in 1994, KLM Properties will operate as KLM Properties ERA Powered, retaining its local identity while gaining access to ERA Real Estate’s technology, marketing resources and referral network.

In a recent development, chaille and Whitney Adkins, who purchased KLM Properties in 2022, bring experience in residential and commercial real estate and construction. Chaille will continue overseeing daily operations in Morgantown.

Ming Tree Realtors, a family-owned brokerage serving California’s Humboldt County since 1972, has affiliated with Century 21 Real Estate.

Now operating as Century 21 Ming Tree, the brokerage maintains offices in Eureka and Fortuna under broker/owner Larry Doss.

A second-generation real estate professional, Doss joined the family business in 1995 before taking over leadership from his father, company co-founder Larry G. Doss. He previously served as president of the Humboldt Association of Realtors in 2007 and was named the Eureka Chamber of Commerce Business Person of the Year in 2015.

Christie’s International Real Estate has named Art Tobani national vice president of affiliate development to accelerate the luxury brokerage network’s expansion across the United States.

Tobani will also help identify growth opportunities for @properties, which has affiliates in six states and Washington, D.C.

Industry observers note that he brings more than 20 years of real estate business development experience, including 12 years in brokerage affiliate sales and advisory services. His work in affiliate recruitment, mergers and acquisitions, and recruiting has generated approximately $12 billion in real estate sales volume.

Naples, Florida-based John R. Wood Properties has rolled out a wellness initiative providing more than 850 agents and staff with individualized coaching focused on personal well-being, resilience and professional development.

Developed in partnership with HatchPath, a Naples-based coaching and wellness platform, the program expands beyond traditional real estate sales coaching to support agents’ personal and professional needs. Unlike conventional coaching focused on production and prospecting, the brokerage is investing in broader well-being services for its workforce.

Compass has added New York City new development specialist Doron Zwickel and his three-person team, who bring more than $1 billion in career sales volume.

Previously affiliated with boutique brokerage CORE, Zwickel has more than 20 years of experience in residential new development and resale. The move expands his team’s reach across Manhattan.

According to recent reports, take Action Team, a Florida-based real estate team led by CEO Mari Parks, has joined Keller Williams Realty Florida Partners in Port Orange, Florida. The team, which includes 13 agents and two staff members, closed 122 transactions totaling $49 million in sales volume in 2025. Parks noted the move will provide agents with additional resources and growth opportunities while maintaining the team’s local expertise and personalized service.

Ledger, a crypto wallet firm, noted it had experienced a security incident related to Optimizely, a third-party service used on its official website, but reassured its consumers about the security of their devices and private keys.

In a post, Ledger stated it was aware of a security incident impacting Optimizely, a third-party service provider used by many other sites as well.

It has been revealed that we are aware of a security incident affecting Optimizely, a third-party service used on https://t.co/d2pWxdG49X, alongside numerous other websites. Our team has remediated the concern, and the malicious code is no longer being served through our website. This incident does not affect the security architecture of Ledger devices. Your private keys remain protected by your Ledger device. For more information from Optimizely: https://t.co/CxzmBxYadb.

Website optimization platform Optimizely noted it had discovered and contained a security incident affecting some of its Web Experimentation customers on November 16, 2026. Optimizely stated that the vulnerable path has now been blocked, the injected code has been removed, and customers have been contacted directly.

Along these lines, Ledger confirmed that its team had remediated the concern and that the malicious code was no longer being served through its website.

Ledger emphasizes that the incident did not affect the security architecture of Ledger devices and that user private keys remain protected by their Ledger device, thus reassuring consumers that the incident had not compromised the core security of its wallet products.

According to researcher Scott Helme, on November 16, 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organizations' websites across several sectors through the Optimizely Web Experimentation platform. The websites included Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger, and Peacock.

Most of the malicious code has now been removed, with only 1 of the 188 infected snippets found, down from 169.

The main point is that trusted JavaScript is not always trustworthy. A third-party dependency can exploit a website without ever breaking the website's own code or infrastructure.

by Kurt Schlosser on Nov 17, 2026 at 7:30 amNovember 17, 2026 at 7:30 am.

Zonar, the Seattle-based fleet tracking company, has a upcoming CEO: Rob Consoli, a longtime tech sales executive who joined the company as chief revenue officer in January.

Consoli is based in Atlanta, but he told GeekWire that Seattle remains Zonar’s headquarters and he has “no intends to change that.” He said he visits the manufacturer’s office in downtown Seattle’s Exchange Building about twice a month.

Recent findings suggest that consoli succeeds Charles Kriete, who led GPS Trackit when the Florida-based company acquired Zonar from German auto supplier Continental in late 2024. Kriete ran the combined company, which is backed by private equity firm Inverness Graham, until September and is now a board advisor.

Consoli previously held revenue chief roles at legal software company Assembly Software, Skuid and Liaison Technologies, which OpenText acquired for $310 million in 2018. He also led North American sales at asset-tracking company I.D. Systems, and started his career as an aerospace engineer at General Dynamics.

Zonar sells GPS tracking hardware, cameras and software that fleet operators use to monitor vehicle location, fuel use and driver behavior, and notes it has more than 400,000 active units installed.

Its biggest market is student transportation. Consoli remarked Zonar serves about half of the school bus market, and its customers also include trucking and delivery fleets such as US Foods, utilities and small businesses.

Sources indicate that zonar’s Seattle-area customers include the Kirkland Police Department, which in 2024 became the first agency to roll out Zonar’s mobile inspection app and GPS asset trackers in its patrol fleet after a pilot program. Officers use the app to complete a digital inspection of their patrol car before each shift, checking tire pressure, emergency equipment such as defibrillators and the rear enclosure used to transport suspects. Each inspection takes two to four minutes, according to the tech giant.

In a recent development, zonar has 409 employees after combining with GPS Trackit, including 70 in Seattle, more than in any other state. Consoli declined to share revenue figures but said Zonar has “more than doubled our profitability in the last 10 months,” helped by upcoming pricing, a reorganized sales team, renegotiated hardware contracts and cost cuts.

It has been revealed that zonar has added 1,000 new customers so far this year, a spokesperson said. Sales to existing customers are running at 118% of the company’s 2026 proposal, while new customer wins are at 97%.

“We’re a very attractive asset in this market right now,” Consoli said.

Zonar competes with larger players including Samsara, Motive and Geotab. Consoli said Zonar sets itself apart through customer service and flexibility. It offers Zonar One, a turnkey system that customers can install the day after ordering, and Zonar Flex, which is customized for large enterprise fleets.

He noted those customers are “not going to get that level of tailoring and customization from any of the massive players.”.

Industry observers note that consoli also wants to lean further into AI. The goal is to send customers proactive alerts instead of making fleet managers dig through dashboards after the fact: a driver running stop signs, a truck off its route, or a school bus running late. Zonar already lets school districts notify parents through an app when a bus is delayed.

“Fleet operators today are really focused on outcomes,” Consoli said. “They want to know that compliance is handled, safety is improved.”.

Founded in Seattle in 2001, Zonar was majority-owned by Continental from 2016 until the 2024 sale. The organization cut 57 jobs in August 2024, when it had more than 300 employees, and made more layoffs after the acquisition.
